title: Deposit Pricing Determination: The Rate a New Certificate of Deposit Term Carries
content:
The rate a new term carries is the tier's published standard interest rate for the term being started, increased by the relationship figure and the jumbo figure the certificate earns on the day the new term is recorded.

## 1. The two figures

The relationship figure is the tier's relationship bonus points when the owner holds an active checking account of a tier the certificate's own tier lists as qualifying, and nothing when the owner holds no such account.

The jumbo figure is the tier's jumbo bonus points when the principal carried into the new term is at least the tier's jumbo threshold, and nothing when it is below that threshold. The principal carried into the new term is the balance standing on the certificate.

## 2. Assembly

The published starting point, the relationship figure and the jumbo figure are added together in that order and the sum is rounded down to the hundredth of a percentage point, once, at the end.

The annual percentage yield the new term carries is the tier's published standard annual percentage yield increased by the same relationship and jumbo figures and rounded the same way.

## 3. The tier, the dates and the markers of the new term

The tier the certificate is carried into is the tier its own renewal target names. The certificate is carried into it with its rate increase used up again for the new term, and the count of terms it has run through rises by one.

The new term starts on the day the term that ended matured and runs for the number of months the tier being renewed into publishes, so that its maturity falls that many calendar months after its start, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist.

## 4. The determination worked through, on hypothetical figures

A certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line stands at 118400.00 USD on the day the new term is recorded. Suppose the tier being started publishes a standard interest rate of 3.70 percent and a standard annual percentage yield of 3.76 percent, relationship bonus points of 0.20 and jumbo bonus points of 0.10, with a jumbo threshold of 100000.00 USD, and suppose the owner holds an active checking account of a qualifying tier.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| principal carried into the new term | 118400.00 USD, the balance standing on the certificate |
| relationship figure | 0.20 points, a qualifying checking account being held |
| jumbo figure | 0.10 points, 118400.00 being at or above 100000.00 |
| published starting point plus the two figures | 3.70 plus 0.20 plus 0.10, giving 4.00 |
| rounded down to the hundredth, once, at the end | 4.00 percent |

The yield follows the same path from 3.76: 3.76 plus 0.20 plus 0.10 gives 4.06, and rounded the same way the new term shows 4.06 percent.

Were the balance instead 82000.00 USD, the jumbo figure would be nothing, the sum would be 3.70 plus 0.20, and the new term would carry 3.90 percent against a yield of 3.96 percent.

## 5. The dates worked through

A term that matured on 31 December and is carried into a tier publishing a term of 6 months starts on 31 December and matures on 30 June, no 31 June existing.
